grades.quote: Thus, read around doesn’t decrease the total number of page faults, but converts many from _major page faults_ (reading disk) to _minor page faults_ (simply updating the page table).
grades.reason: Covers page-fault cost and spatial locality in clustered paging or prepaging. Page-granular strided access can cause many page faults, and the passage explains major versus minor faults. It never addresses page-stride array access, TLB misses or cache conflicts, so it gives only limited background.
Textbook exercises on PAE page-table geometry and replacement policies. Nothing here explains why accesses one page apart would be slow.
About disk-space external fragmentation and file allocation, not memory access strides or paging performance.
Describes the linear page table structure and its size. It does not discuss TLB misses, page faults or any slowdown from page-strided access, so it doesn't help with the query.
